viva.question: What's the difference between an ordinary point and a regular singular point?
viva.answer: At an ordinary point, p and q are analytic; at a regular singular point, p,q may blow up, but (x-x0)p(x) and (x-x0)^2 q(x) remain analytic.
viva.why: This weaker condition is exactly what the Frobenius method needs, since it allows a controlled singularity.
viva.followUp: Which method applies at a regular singular point instead of the ordinary power series method?
viva.trap: Confusing ordinary and regular singular points when classifying a given ODE.

viva.question: Why does the Laplace method avoid finding arbitrary constants separately?
viva.answer: Initial conditions are plugged in directly during the transform step, so the resulting algebraic equation already encodes them.
viva.why: Classical solution methods find a general solution first and then solve for constants afterward; Laplace builds them in from the start.
viva.followUp: What kind of forcing term is the Laplace method especially good at handling?
viva.trap: Forgetting to include initial-condition terms when transforming derivatives.
